left.definition: Location near or direction toward the left side.

right.definition: The side opposite the left; here a direction.

straight.definition: Continuing in one direction without turning.

forward.definition: At or near or directed toward the front.

backward.exampleUsage: Step backward away from the table.

up.definition: Towards a higher place or position.
up.exampleUsage: Go up to the next floor.

down.definition: Towards a lower place or position.

turn.definition: To change the direction in which you are facing or moving.

stop.definition: To cease moving or bring movement to an end.

go.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.

north.definition: The direction toward the North Pole.
north.exampleUsage: The park is north of the station.

south.exampleUsage: The office is south of the park.

east.definition: The cardinal direction opposite west, to the right when facing north.
east.exampleUsage: The library is east of the station.

west.definition: The cardinal direction opposite east, to the left when facing north.
west.exampleUsage: The school is west of the park.

northeast.definition: The compass point midway between north and east.
northeast.exampleUsage: The museum is northeast of the square.

northwest.definition: The compass point midway between north and west.
northwest.exampleUsage: The park is northwest of the station.

southeast.definition: The compass point midway between south and east.
southeast.exampleUsage: The office is southeast of the square.

southwest.definition: The compass point midway between south and west.
southwest.exampleUsage: The school is southwest of the library.

compass.definition: An instrument used to find directions, commonly with a magnetic needle.
compass.exampleUsage: Nora checks the direction with a compass.

direction.definition: The way towards which someone or something faces or moves.
direction.exampleUsage: Nora asks which direction to go.

near.exampleUsage: The café is near the station.

far.definition: At a great distance from a person, place, or object.
far.exampleUsage: The hospital is far from the station.

close.definition: Near in distance; here close to a place.
close.exampleUsage: The park is close to the café.

nearby.definition: Not far away; in the area near a place.

distant.exampleUsage: The tower looks distant from here.

here.definition: At this place or in this location.
here.exampleUsage: Please wait here beside the desk.

there.exampleUsage: The entrance is there beside the tree.

everywhere.definition: In all places or throughout an area.
everywhere.exampleUsage: There are trees everywhere in this park.

nowhere.definition: In or to no place; not anywhere.
nowhere.exampleUsage: Nora can find her keys nowhere in the room.

somewhere.exampleUsage: The keys are somewhere in the bag.

intersection.definition: A place where two or more roads meet or cross.
intersection.exampleUsage: Two roads meet at the intersection.

corner.definition: The place where two streets or edges meet; here a street corner.
corner.exampleUsage: Nora waits at the street corner.

block.definition: An area of buildings enclosed by streets, often used to describe walking distance.
block.exampleUsage: The office is one block from the station.

crosswalk.definition: A marked part of a road intended for pedestrians to cross.

traffic-light.definition: A signalling device with lights used to control road traffic.
traffic-light.exampleUsage: The traffic light controls vehicles at the junction.

roundabout.definition: A circular road junction where traffic moves around a central island.
roundabout.exampleUsage: The road goes around the island at the roundabout.

one-way.definition: Allowing traffic to travel in only one direction; here a one-way street.
one-way.exampleUsage: Vehicles travel in one direction on the one-way street.

dead-end.definition: A street that ends without joining another street.
dead-end.exampleUsage: The dead end has no road continuing beyond it.

highway.definition: A main road, especially one used for longer-distance travel.
highway.exampleUsage: The highway connects the two towns.

sidewalk.definition: A path beside a road intended for pedestrians; American English for pavement.

building.definition: A structure that has a roof and walls and stands more or less permanently in one place.
building.exampleUsage: The office is in that building.

bridge.definition: A structure carrying a road or path across an obstacle such as a river.

monument.definition: A structure erected to commemorate persons or events.
monument.exampleUsage: The monument commemorates a historic event.

fountain.definition: A structure that sends water upward and lets it fall back down.

statue.definition: A three-dimensional figure of a person, animal or other subject.
statue.exampleUsage: The statue stands in the square.

tower.definition: A tall narrow building or structure.
tower.exampleUsage: The tower rises above the other buildings.

church.definition: A building used for Christian worship.
church.exampleUsage: The church is beside the square.

park.definition: A public outdoor area used for walking, relaxing, and recreation.
park.exampleUsage: Nora visits the park after work.

school.definition: A place or institution where people receive education.
school.exampleUsage: The school is near the community centre.

hospital.definition: A place where people receive medical care, sometimes while staying there.
hospital.exampleUsage: The hospital is across from the park.
